results.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets Claude approve routine pull requests - The New Stack
results.content:
Anthropic bills by the token. At Code Review’s launch in March, the company put the average cost at $15 to $25 per review (which isn’t exactly cheap, but cheaper than shipping broken code…).

Running `/ship` counts as regular Claude Code usage, and while Claude Approvals has no base charge of its own, classifiers consume billable tokens just like any other model use. Policies that call for Code Review trigger a paid review, even in observe-only mode.

There is a bit of a trial period, though. Eligible Enterprise customers have until Jan. 15, 2027, to claim “at least” $10,000 in Claude Ship credits, Anthropic says, but they have to use them within 30 days of claiming those credits. [...] For a while now, Anthropic has been saying that Claude already writes most of the code for Claude Code. The slow part, the company argues, now comes after a developer opens a PR. By the time the review comes back, that developer may have already moved on to something else. This means even a minor change means putting that work aside to push a fix, wait for the checks to run again, and track down someone to approve it.

Most companies don’t work at the pace of Anthropic, but the bottleneck of code reviews — and the DevOps lifecycle in general — is something that slows down virtually all businesses at this point.

## Who has to sign off? [...] ## How Anthropic uses Claude Ship

Anthropic says the Claude Code team uses Claude Ship on many of its own PRs. When a customer flagged a misleading passage in the Analytics API docs, for example, a product manager asked Claude

Tag, the company’s Slack agent, about it. Tag opened a PR, Code Review found nothing blocking it, and a docs reviewer signed off. The fix merged that evening.

From June to September, the company says, the team more than doubled the number of PRs it merged while the share it reverted fell by more than 40 percent.

It’s worth noting, though, that Claude Ship covers only part of that overall process. The team’s own engineering post from October, for example, also describes a separate security review that can block a merge.

results.title: Introducing Claude Ship | Claude by Anthropic
results.content:
### How the Claude Code team ships

We run Claude Ship on many of our own pull requests. One of the biggest changes is who can act on customer feedback. For example, a product manager on the Claude Code team can now read a piece of feedback, talk through ideas and tradeoffs with Claude Tag, have it open a PR, and move on to the next thing while Claude Ship takes it through review, fixes, and an approval decision.

Recently, a customer was confused because our Analytics API documentation implied an Admin key could pull Pro and Team usage. The PM asked Claude Tag whether a fix was in flight, and it opened one. Code Review found nothing blocking, a docs reviewer signed off, Claude Approvals passed, and the fix merged that same evening.

### What customers are saying [...] Claude Ship is not available to organizations with Zero Data Retention, the HIPAA configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys.

### Get started

Developers can update Claude Code and run `/ship` on their next change. `/ship` is rolling out in Claude Code and the desktop app starting today.

Teams already using Code Review can add PR Steward on a repository, and an approval policy in observe mode.

Teams new to Code Review can read the setup guide to connect GitHub and turn on their first repository.

Learn more in documentation. [...] ### What customers are saying

> “We have had numerous cases where Claude Code Review caught real issues before a human reviewer got to the pull request, and PR Steward helped the contributor fix them. Our reviewers were already using Claude Code to keep up with the volume, so having Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals start automatically when a pull request opens makes that simpler. We keep a human in the loop, and the human’s time now goes to the changes that need it.”

> “PR Steward is helping teams in our pilot spend less time working through code review feedback and more time building. We can tailor it to our teams’ processes, including how it suggests changes and organizes feedback. That flexibility has made it a useful part of the development workflow.”

results.title: Claude Code didn't get worse. The harness did. And that ends one of the most common AI complaints of 2026. - DEV Community
results.content:
DEV Community

## DEV Community

Anil Kurmi

Posted on May 16

# Claude Code didn't get worse. The harness did. And that ends one of the most common AI complaints of 2026.

For two months, the same complaint kept showing up on every developer forum I read: Claude Code feels worse. Sometimes worded politely, sometimes not. The vibe was unanimous enough that I almost started believing it on reputation alone.

Then on April 23, Anthropic published a postmortem that I think ends this whole class of complaint as a useful conversation. Read it. Even if you don't ship anything with Claude. Especially then. [...] Here's the position I'll defend: "the model got worse" is no longer a credible developer complaint without evidence. The Anthropic postmortem is proof that the user experience of an LLM product can degrade severely without anyone touching the weights. From now on, the responsible reply to "Claude feels worse this week" is show me the harness diff, not the model card.

## What actually broke

The thing that should make every AI product engineer sit up: none of the three regressions were model weights. They were all in the layer most teams treat as boring infrastructure. [...] Regression 1 — reasoning depth got quietly downgraded. On March 4, Anthropic moved the default reasoning effort from `high` to `medium` to cut latency. Users reported lower intelligence. The complaints were real. The model was the same. The default wasn't. They reverted on April 7.

`high`
`medium`

Regression 2 — a caching bug ate prior reasoning. On March 26, an intended one-time clearing of old thinking in stale sessions was applied repeatedly. So context kept getting amputated mid-conversation. The model felt forgetful because it actually was forgetting. Fixed April 10.

results.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review, fix and approve pull requests under team-set rules | MLQ.ai
results.content:
Anthropic on Monday introduced Claude Ship, a system that takes pull requests through review, fixes and an approval decision, with teams setting the rules for which changes still need a person to sign off [\[1\]]( Reuters reported the launch the same day, saying the product is available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for projects on GitHub [\[2\]](

Anthropic describes Claude Ship as being in beta overall. It combines an existing review tool with two new beta features [\[1\]](

## What each part does

Code Review, which is generally available, reviews pull requests from several angles, checks its own findings adversarially, sorts them and posts them on the pull request. Each repository can choose Quick, Standard or Deep review [\[1\]]( [...] ## How teams turn it on

Developers can run /ship in Claude Code to push a change, open a pull request and handle review and feedback; the command is rolling out in Claude Code and the desktop app [\[1\]]( Admins enable Code Review and PR Steward per repository, set review level, timing and spend limits, and Claude Approvals starts once a policy file exists on the default branch. Claude Ship works with existing branch protection and required checks [\[1\]](

It is not available to organizations using Zero Data Retention, Anthropic's HIPAA configuration or customer-managed encryption keys [\[1\]](

## Pricing and early results [...] # Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review, fix and approve pull requests under team-set rules

- Claude Ship has three parts: Code Review (generally available), PR Steward (beta) and Claude Approvals (beta) [\[1\]](
- Claude Approvals follows a policy file in the repository and can auto-approve routine changes or require a human [\[1\]](
- Available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repositories; not for organizations using Zero Data Retention, the HIPAA configuration or customer-managed keys [\[1\]](
- Billing is token-based with admin spend limits; eligible Enterprise customers can claim at least $10,000 in credits until Jan. 15, 2027 [\[1\]](
